h2: Tank inspection around Baton Rouge: river terminals, storm season and keeping the API 653 cycle
html:
Tank inspection around Baton Rouge: river terminals, storm season and keeping the API 653 cycle

Storage tank inspection around Baton Rouge serves refinery and chemical tank farms and river terminals along the Mississippi. Atlantis performs the NDE for the owner's API 653 program, including MFL floor scanning, UT shell thickness, vacuum box testing and settlement data, plus post-storm condition checks. Acceptance and the inspection report stay with the owner's API 653 inspector, and Atlantis does not sign as inspector of record.

A river of tankage. The Port of South Louisiana runs along 54 miles of the Mississippi between New Orleans and Baton Rouge and handled 248.1 million short tons in 2023, with chemicals and petroleum products among its cargoes. Terminal operators on this corridor handle many products in tanks that change service often, and every change of service is a point at which API 653 asks for an engineering review of the tank's suitability, including a brittle fracture check where applicable.

Checks after a storm. From June through the end of November, Gulf storms are the main event risk for river tank farms. API 653 sets routine and internal inspection intervals, but most owners' programs add an event-driven inspection after a hurricane or flood. Typical post-storm items are:

  • Floating roofs: pontoon compartments for water or product, roof drain function, seal damage and any tilt or hang-up
  • Shell: buckling or local deformation of tanks that were near empty when the wind loaded them
  • Foundations: washout, ringwall cracking and any shift of a tank that floodwater lifted at low liquid level
  • Appurtenances: stairways, platforms, nozzles and secondary containment walls

Recording those checks against the same reference points used in routine inspections lets the owner's inspector separate storm damage from older defects, which also matters when insurers ask for evidence.

Floors on wet ground. A high water table and fine river-delta soils keep the underside of tank bottoms damp, so soil-side corrosion is a common cause of floor thinning there. MFL scanning finds where the plate has thinned from either side, and UT prove-up of each indication gives the depth the API 653 floor calculation needs. Release prevention barriers and cathodic protection change the expected rate, so their condition belongs in the report.

Rules. In Louisiana, federal OSHA enforces process safety management, and a tank inside a covered process falls under that standard's mechanical integrity element. Terminals storing oil above the federal SPCC thresholds must also follow their 40 CFR Part 112 plan, which ties tank integrity testing to an industry standard. A guide to how the NDE supports the owner's inspector is on the API 653 tank NDE support page, and local detail is on API 653 tank inspection in Baton Rouge.

For the services themselves, see aboveground storage tank inspection, MFL floor scanning and, for vacuum box work, leak testing. Atlantis ERP keeps floor maps and shell readings tied to fixed locations so the next campaign can be compared directly. To plan routine or post-storm work, send the tank list, products and access dates through the Baton Rouge tank inspection request.
